A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAP study, with matching authors, central method, and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Rainbow and DER experiments on Atari, Atari100K, and Procgen, together with architectural comparisons, training diagnostics, and appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds SAC experiments on DMC, DrQ variants on Atari100K, and additional architectural and sparsity analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains spatial averaging of each encoder feature map before the dense layers, as specified in Equation 1. Applying GAP to additional agents and testing architectural variants does not introduce a new GAP component or learning objective.

E1.justification: v2 adds pixel-based continuous-control evaluation on DMC: cartpole-swingup, cheetah-run, walker-walk, and walker-stand (Figure 11). This substantially extends task and action-space coverage beyond v1's discrete-action Atari and Procgen environments, which remain included.

E2.justification: v2 adds paired baseline-versus-GAP comparisons using DrQ and DrQ(epsilon) on Atari100K and SAC on DMC. The principal Figure 10 comparator set remains unchanged: pruning, RigL, static sparsity, SoftMoE-1, weight decay, layer normalization, and the baseline.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce SAC with eightfold actor/critic embedding scaling, 80% and 95% sparsity settings beyond the existing 90%, fourfold encoder-width scaling with an unscaled dense head, and a sweep through three additional dense layers. These substantially expand evaluation settings; the existing Atari hyperparameters in Table 1 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds a deeper-encoder control without dense-head scaling. Appendix C adds sparsity sensitivity for pruning and static networks, isolated encoder-width scaling, and a broader dense-layer depth sweep (Figures 12, 15, and 16). These test the bottleneck explanation under substantially more controls and architectural conditions. The earlier max-pooling analysis is retained as Figure 14.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent seeds and 95% stratified bootstrap confidence intervals, with the same aggregate reporting practice. The added checklist repeats this information; it does not establish additional runs or a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds performance curves for SAC/DMC and DrQ variants, a deeper-encoder control, and sparsity, encoder-width, and dense-depth results. The new depth sweep shows GAP remaining above the corresponding baseline even as performance declines with greater depth. These are substantial added findings under additional settings; the principal matched v1 results are retained.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 adds the expectation operator missing from v1's definition of the action-value function, making a limited formal correction. The GAP equation and parameter-count expressions remain unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: the encoder-to-dense bottleneck limits scaling, existing architectural methods implicitly target it, and GAP offers a simpler, efficient intervention. The expanded experiments provide additional support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4 changes the interpretation of Figure 10 from outperforming all methods to performance comparable to SoftMoE with greater simplicity and efficiency. It also adds discussion of possible spatial-information loss from aggressive pooling. The stated limitations concerning non-pixel environments and architectures without a clear bottleneck remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the SAC CNN architecture reference and eightfold actor/critic embedding scaling, plus the configurations of its new sparsity and architectural sweeps. Existing Rainbow/DER hyperparameters, libraries, hardware, and access links remain unchanged. No new code release is documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for scaling laws, SAC, DMC, and the two Yarats papers supporting the added experiments. Its positioning relative to MoE, sparse training, and concurrent pooling approaches remains substantially unchanged; the updated publication information for Trumpp et al. is not a new cited work.

P1.justification: Background and experimental-setup passages are substantially rewritten and expanded. SoftMoE and sparse networks become subsections under Network scaling, Section 4's discussion is reordered, and a NeurIPS checklist and broader-impacts appendix are added. This is substantial editorial and structural revision despite retaining the overall scientific argument.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS template replaces the DeepMind layout, with extensive figure resizing and relocation. Figure 5 changes from side-by-side to stacked panels, Figure 4 gains a series, Figure 11 gains a DMC row, and four new appendix figures appear. Several legends and axes are revised; the existing hyperparameter table and per-game plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The continuous-control and additional-agent evaluations substantially strengthen evidence for generality beyond v1's discrete-action experiments. The added encoder control and sparsity/depth sweeps also test the central bottleneck explanation across previously unchecked conditions. Together these materially strengthen the empirical case, although added-agent specifications remain brief and the existing disagreement between four added encoder blocks in Section 3.2 and two in the experimental appendix remains unresolved.
